newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ profit to reflect competition, high NZ dlr.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ profit to reflect competition, high NZ dlr.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd is expected to report an annual profit towards the upper end of its own forecast range of NZ$221-234 million (US$153-162 million) next week, aviation analysts said on Tuesday.
They also expect the national flag carrier to maintain its total fully imputed annual dividend of 20 NZ cents.
Of more interest will be signs of any movement with its plan to buy half of Ansett Airlines from Australia's TNT Ltd as a decision from Australia's Foreign Investment Review (FIRB) board draws near.

The future profitability of Ansett would also be an issue after TNT's partner in Ansett, News Corp Ltd, said last week that Ansett had made a loss in the June year. Ansett on Tuesday announced a A$150 million ($118 million) cost cutting drive over the next two years.

Air NZ made a record NZ$260.2 million net profit in the year to June 1995, but the year just passed was one in which the company endured a very strong New Zealand dollar, increased competition and slower tourism growth.
Kevin Bennett at Doyle Paterson Brown said he would be surprised to see the result waver outside the forecast range.
Key elements in the announcement would be yields, the exact impact of the New Zealand dollar, load factors, the airline's ability to fill planes, and cost containment.
"You've had quite vivid examples of how you can get still get earnings growth despite slightly softer than anticipated revenues. That has been a bit of a trend worldwide," he said.
Bennett said he did not think the impact of cut-price operator Kiwi International would be material to the result.
"Kiwi has stimulated the market sufficiently to bring a new clientele on board, so it has not been a material player on Air NZ's profitability."
But the price war has hotted up since balance date, with Qantas Airways weighing in with aggressive pricing initiatives which may have an impact on the current year.
Mary Watson at brokers First NZ Capital expects a result of around NZ$225 million.
Watson expected a 7.5 percent erosion of yields, due mostly to competitive pressures. "If there was less than this I would be delighted. If there was more I would cut my 1997 forecasts."
Air NZ had done well at peggging back costs in the first half and would do well to repeat the performance in the second.

"Obviously a worst-case scenario would be if yields were weaker than expected and costs were higher. I think they will do okay on the costs side, despite the fact the fuel prices quite a bit over the last six months."

The Australian FIRB has until the end of September to announce its decision on Ansett. Air NZ, which is 42.5 percent owned by Brierley Investments Ltd and 19.9 percent by Qantas, reports its result on Monday.
